data.title: Japanese population below 120 million for first time in decades
data.description: TOKYO - The number of Japanese people living in the country has fallen below 120 million for the first time in 42 years, government data showed Wednesday, as the nation confronts a low birth rate and an ageing society.

data.title: Crisis-hit Cuba opens pharmacies, gas stations to private firms
data.description: HAVANA - Cuba moved to open crisis-ravaged parts of the state-run economy to private firms Wednesday, as the communist government struggles to ease acute shortages resulting from a US energy blockade.

data.title: Idi Amin's grandson disqualified from Commonwealth boxing bout
data.description: GLASGOW - The grandson of former Ugandan president Idi Amin saw his bid for Commonwealth boxing gold end in disgrace as Aziz Abdul was disqualified for a headbutt in his quarter-final on Wednesday.

data.title: Principal reaction to FIFA's private investor plan
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - FIFA's plans to sell a stake in the business operations of the World Cup and its other competitions through the creation of a semi-private subsidiary has sparked disbelief and outrage globally.

data.title: O'Connor wins Commonwealth heptathlon as Australia set new record for swimming golds
data.description: GLASGOW - Kate O'Connor cruised to heptathlon gold for Northern Ireland as Australia rounded off their best ever Commonwealth Games in the pool with nine more swimming gold medals on Wednesday for a total of 37.

data.title: AI strategy now 'falling behind'
data.description: Thailand must develop its own Thai-language AI systems or risk falling behind foreign technology companies, economists and digital policy experts have warned.

data.title: Water security fears grow
data.description: A series of emerging reports in recent weeks concerning tight water supplies and river pollution in central and northern Thailand mean the nation is now facing a challenging water security situation, experts say.

data.title: Supanida snaps losing run to reach last 16
data.description: Supanida Katethong finally ended her first round losing spell when the Thai left-hander won her opening match at the US$250,000 (approx 8.4 million baht) BWF Taipei Open on Wednesday.

data.title: Thailand back to hard graft after day off
data.description: Thailand's national team were back on the training pitch at BGTC 3 on Wednesday, stepping up preparations for their Group B second fixture against Malaysia in the Asean Hyundai Cup 2026.

data.title: Ministry pushes Chumphon-Ranong rail
data.description: The Transport Ministry has pushed for the Chumphon-Ranong double-track railway project, describing the 110-kilometre route as a missing link needed to connect Thailand's rail network with an Andaman Sea port.

data.title: Flood diversion canal hits new flak
data.description: A civic network in Nakhon Nayok is stepping up its campaign against the proposed Pasak–Gulf of Thailand flood diversion canal, accusing authorities of misrepresenting the outcome of public consultations and downplaying strong local resistance to the project.

data.title: Dialogue offers path to peace
data.description: Manila: Thailand and Cambodia should engage more at diplomatic levels to resolve ongoing conflicts, said Asean secretary-general Kao Kim Hourn.

data.title: BTS pulls out of Grammys after Asian pop category introduction
data.description: SEOUL - Global K-pop sensation BTS said on Wednesday they will not submit their music for next year's Grammy Awards, following the Recording Academy's introduction of new categories that include the Best Asian Pop Music Performance.

data.title: No Thais hurt in Japan quake
data.description: The Foreign Affairs Ministry has activated emergency contact channels for Thai citizens in Japan following the magnitude 7.1 earthquake that struck Kumamoto Prefecture on Tuesday.

data.title: Asean envoy plans to visit Myanmar
data.description: Manila: Theresa P Lazaro, secretary of foreign affairs of the Philippines and the Asean Chair's Special Envoy on Myanmar, said she is scheduled to make a humanitarian visit to Myanmar in the fourth quarter of this year.

data.title: OPDC eyes some branch office closures
data.description: The Office of the Public Sector Development Commission (OPDC) will propose closing provincial branch offices of state agencies as part of an overhaul of the public administration system.

data.title: Spanish wildfire evacuees go home as France hit by new heat alert
data.description: ALDEA DEL FRESNO (SPAIN) - Thousands who fled huge wildfires in Spain returned home on Wednesday while in France firefighters braced for worsening conditions in their own battle with raging flames.

data.title: Nigeria dismantles meth lab, but fears of Mexican cartel links linger
data.description: IJEBU ODE (NIGERIA) - The cooking cauldrons and vats of chemicals were left behind in an abandoned shed, hidden in a Nigerian forest -- remnants of an alleged multimillion-dollar transnational meth operation.

data.title: Survivors still sought as Japan quake death toll hits 13
data.description: YATSUSHIRO, Japan - Rescuers frantically searched for ‌survivors on Wednesday, a day after a 7.1-magnitude earthquake shook southern Japan, killing at least 13 people, knocking out power to thousands of homes and rupturing roads across the region.

data.title: Oscar-winning musician Glen Hansard dies in motorcycle crash
data.description: DUBLIN - The Irish musician Glen Hansard, who won a Best Original Song Oscar in 2008 for the indie film “Once”, died in a motorcycle crash at the age ​of 56 early on ⁠Wednesday, his management company said.
